profile.name: Nandha Gopal M
profile.tagline: I write the firmware that makes machines move on time.
profile.specialization: ESP32 · STM32 · FreeRTOS · Motion control · Industrial HMI
profile.availability: Open to embedded / firmware roles — available to join immediately
bio: I build firmware for machines that have to behave the same way on the thousandth cycle as on the first: step pulses that stay in time, limit switches that always abort, screens an operator can use without a manual.

Before engineering college I spent two years at a Xiaomi service centre doing board-level repair — power ICs, charging circuits, recovering bricked phones. That is where I learned to read a schematic, trust a multimeter over a guess, and work from the symptom back to the cause. I now do the same thing across firmware, sensors and HMI on industrial automation equipment.

experience.summary: Worked across hardware, firmware and HMI on deployed gantry-based industrial automation systems, and on firmware for a dip coating machine.
highlights: Traced faults on deployed machines down to the layer that actually caused them — wiring, sensor, firmware, communication or HMI — instead of replacing parts by guess.
Wrote and debugged ESP32 firmware for an automated dip coating system: process sequencing, motor control, sensor feedback and UART/SPI/I2C peripheral drivers.
Split concurrent work across FreeRTOS tasks — motion, sensor monitoring, process timing and UI — so a slow screen redraw can never stall a motion step.
Verified signals on the bench with a logic analyser and serial instrumentation before blaming the code, and re-tested the machine after every corrective change.

experience.summary: Board-level diagnosis and repair of Android smartphones, under warranty turnaround pressure.
highlights: Diagnosed motherboard-level failures, mostly around power ICs and charging circuits, using schematics and measurement rather than part swapping.
Flashed firmware and recovered bricked devices, including data recovery for customers who had no backup.

projects.title: Industrial dip coater controller
projects.subtitle: Dual-ESP32 machine controller with a 7-inch touch HMI
projects.description: A dip coating machine needs a coating run to be repeatable: the same immersion depth, the same dwell, the same withdrawal speed, every cycle. The controller splits that job across two ESP32s — one running the operator screen, one running motion — so the UI can never delay a step pulse.
highlights: Step pulse generation off a hardware timer, so motion timing is independent of what the UI thread is doing
Recipes stored as JSON on SD card — an operator saves a process once and replays it
Interrupt-driven limit switches, jog boundaries and an emergency abort path that runs before anything else
Backend link over UART/USB serial and Wi-Fi sockets, with mDNS discovery so the screen finds the controller on its own

projects.title: Gantry motion control
projects.subtitle: XY stage firmware — homing, jog, coordinated moves
projects.description: Firmware for a belt-and-leadscrew XY gantry: homing against limit switches, manual jog with soft boundaries, and coordinated moves driven by a step/direction interface into TB6600 drivers.
highlights: Homing routine that establishes a known origin before any commanded move is accepted
Soft limits in software plus hard limit switches on interrupt — two independent stops
Serial command interface so the motion layer can be driven and tested from a laptop

media.caption: XY stage with leadscrew, belt axis and limit switches
Bench test — motion commands driven from serial
Stepper, driver and controller wired for step timing checks

projects.title: Driver monitoring & alcohol detection
projects.subtitle: STM32 sensing with a vision dashboard on the host
projects.description: A safety system that watches the driver and the cabin at the same time: an MQ-3 alcohol sensor read through the ADC on an STM32, drowsiness detection running on a host PC from a webcam, and a dashboard that raises the alert.
highlights: ADC sampling and threshold logic on the microcontroller, so detection does not depend on the PC staying alive
Framed UART link between firmware and the Python backend
Dashboard showing live sensor values, camera feed and alert state together

media.caption: STM32 pin map — ADC, UART and alert wiring for the monitoring board
Monitoring dashboard — sensor gauges and alert state
Test rig: sensor board, motor load and live dashboard
Alert raised when the alcohol threshold is crossed

projects.title: Network-level phishing blocker
projects.subtitle: Raspberry Pi appliance doing DNS filtering
projects.description: A Raspberry Pi sitting between the LAN and the internet, running Pi-hole to drop known malicious domains at DNS level, with blocklists and health checks kept current by cron-driven Bash scripts.
highlights: DNS-level filtering, so every device on the network is covered without installing anything on it
Scheduled blocklist refresh and service health checks with logging

media.caption: Pi-hole dashboard — live query count, block rate and client health
Network diagram — Raspberry Pi acting as the DNS sinkhole
Raspberry Pi appliance layout with blocklists and filtering logic

recommendation.quote: Worked through faults layer by layer on live industrial systems, and could tell whether the cause sat in the hardware, the firmware, a sensor, the communication link or the HMI.
